Package io.github.jspinak.brobot.annotations

Annotation Interface OutgoingTransition

@Target(METHOD) @Retention(RUNTIME) @Documented public @interface OutgoingTransition
Marks a method as an OutgoingTransition - a transition FROM the state defined in the enclosing @TransitionSet class TO a specific target state.

This annotation represents the cleaner pattern where a state's transition class contains its incoming transition (IncomingTransition) and all its outgoing transitions. This is more cohesive since outgoing transitions use the current state's images.

Special State Markers: The 'to' parameter can accept special marker classes for dynamic transitions:

  • PreviousState.class - Returns to the most recently hidden state (for overlays, dialogs, menus)
  • CurrentState.class - Self-transition that stays in or re-enters the current state
  • ExpectedState.class - (Future) Runtime-determined target state

Hidden States: When a state overlays another (e.g., a menu opening over a page), the covered state is automatically tracked as "hidden". Transitions to PreviousState.class will dynamically resolve to return to whatever state was hidden.

The annotated method should:

  • Return boolean (true if transition succeeds, false otherwise)
  • Contain the actions needed to navigate TO the target state
  • Be a member of a class annotated with @TransitionSet
  • Use images from the current state (defined in @TransitionSet)

Example usage: 


 // Simple transition to a specific state
 @OutgoingTransition(activate = {PricingState.class})  // pathCost defaults to 1
 public boolean toPricing() {
     log.info("Navigating from Homepage to Pricing");
     return action.click(homepageState.getPricingLink()).isSuccess();
 }

 // Return to hidden state (dynamic transition)
 @OutgoingTransition(
     activate = {PreviousState.class},  // Returns to whatever state was covered
     pathCost = 0,
     description = "Close modal and return to previous state"
 )
 public boolean closeModal() {
     return action.click(modalState.getCloseButton()).isSuccess();
 }

 // Self-transition (stays in current state)
 @OutgoingTransition(
     activate = {CurrentState.class},  // Stay in or re-enter current state
     pathCost = 2,
     description = "Load more results"
 )
 public boolean loadMore() {
     return action.click(loadMoreButton).isSuccess();
 }

 // Modal overlay - keep origin visible
 @OutgoingTransition(
     activate = {SettingsModalState.class},
     staysVisible = true,  // dashboard remains visible behind modal
     pathCost = 2
 )
 public boolean toSettingsModal() {
     return action.click(dashboardState.getSettingsButton()).isSuccess();
 }

 // Complex transition with multiple state changes
 @OutgoingTransition(
     activate = {DashboardState.class, SidebarState.class, HeaderState.class},
     exit = {LoginState.class},
     staysVisible = false,  // originating state is deactivated (default)
     pathCost = 0  // preferred path (lower cost)
 )
 public boolean toDashboard() {
     return action.click(loginState.getLoginButton()).isSuccess();
 }

  • Element Details

    • activate

      Class<?>[] activate
      States to activate during this transition. This transition will navigate FROM the state defined in @TransitionSet and activate all states in this array.

      Can include:

      • Regular state classes (e.g., HomeState.class)
      • PreviousState.class - Returns to the most recently hidden state
      • CurrentState.class - Self-transition or re-enters current state
      • ExpectedState.class - (Future) Runtime-determined state

      For single-target transitions, use a single-element array: activate = {TargetState.class}

      For multi-state transitions, include all states to activate: activate = {MainState.class, SidePanel.class, Header.class}

      Returns:
      array of state classes to activate (required, must have at least one)

    • exit

      Class<?>[] exit
      States to exit/deactivate during this transition. Note: The originating state's deactivation is controlled by staysVisible.
      Returns:
      array of state classes to exit
      Default:
      {}

    • staysVisible

      boolean staysVisible
      Whether the originating state remains visible after transition. Default is false (originating state is deactivated).
      Returns:
      true if originating state should remain visible, false otherwise
      Default:
      false

    • pathCost

      int pathCost
      Path-finding cost for this transition. The total cost of a path is the sum of all state costs and transition costs in that path. Lower costs are preferred when multiple paths exist. Higher costs discourage using this transition in pathfinding. Default is 1.

      Example uses:

      • 0 - Free transition (no cost)
      • 1 - Normal transition (default)
      • 5 - Slightly expensive transition
      • 10+ - Expensive/fallback transition
      Returns:
      the path cost for this transition
      Default:
      1

    • description

      String description
      Optional description of this transition. Useful for documentation and debugging.
      Returns:
      the transition description
      Default:
      ""
